title: The Tokio/Rayon Trap and Why Async/Await Fails Concurrency
summary: This article explores the pitfalls of combining Tokio (Rust's async runtime) and Rayon (parallelism library), arguing that async/await complicates rather than simplifies concurrency by forcing developers into awkward compromises between blocking parallelism and async execution.
problem_solved: Addresses the misconception that async/await elegantly solves concurrency problems, exposing the friction when mixing blocking parallelism with async code.
why_valuable: Provides deep insights into Rust's concurrency model trade-offs, helping systems developers avoid common architectural mistakes when designing high-performance async applications.
